finding.claim: The /logo handler validates the logo URL with a substring check (strings.Contains(raw, "example.io")) rather than a hostname check, then fetches it with http.Get, following redirects. An attacker can reach internal hosts or cloud metadata and receive the response body.
finding.source: main.go:31 r.FormValue("logo"), unauthenticated route registered at main.go:43
finding.sink: main.go:36 http.Get(raw); response streamed back at main.go:38

trace.note: /logo route registered with no auth middleware
raw taken directly from the logo form/query parameter
strings.Contains substring check on the raw string; not a hostname check
http.Get(raw) with default client, follows up to 10 redirects, no IP/private-range block
io.Copy streams full upstream response to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: Substring check at main.go:32 (bypassable: http://169.254.169.254/?example.io, http://127.0.0.1:8081/?example.io, http://attacker.test/x?example.io redirecting internally). No scheme restriction beyond Go transport http/https. No private-IP blocking. Redirects not restricted. /cdn handler (main.go:14-28) checked and SAFE: exact Hostname() map match at main.go:20 plus noRedirect at main.go:12/24.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is the substring test at main.go:32 (strings.Contains(raw, "example.io")), which is not a closing guard. No hostname set match, anchored match, or private-IP block exists between main.go:31 and main.go:36. The /cdn handler's exact-hostname map check at main.go:20 and noRedirect at main.go:12 do not apply to /logo.
verdict.reason: The raw value from r.FormValue("logo") at main.go:31 is unauthenticated (route registered without middleware at main.go:43), passes only the substring test at main.go:32, is fetched with the default http.Get at main.go:36 (redirects followed, no IP restriction), and the body is streamed back at main.go:38, so an attacker can use URLs like http://169.254.169.254/?example.io to read internal responses.
